test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-II Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2025)
subject: general
question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 99 min and 90 min, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 50 min. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the tank take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM(99, 90, 50) = 4950 units.

Efficiency of A = 4950 ÷ 99 = 50 units/min.

Efficiency of B = 4950 ÷ 90 = 55 units/min.

Net efficiency of (A + B + C) = 4950 ÷ 50 = 99 units/min.

Efficiency of C = 99 − (50 + 55) = −6 units/min.

Time taken by C = 4950 ÷ 6 = 825 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 825 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the cistern = 99 min

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the cistern = 90 min

Time taken by all three pipes (A + B + C) to fill the cistern = 50 min

**Concept Used:**

Total capacity = LCM of individual time taken

Efficiency = Total capacity ÷ Time taken

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of emptying Pipe C be E꜀.

⇒ Total Efficiency = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B + Efficiency of C

⇒ 99 = 50 + 55 + E꜀

⇒ 99 = 105 + E꜀

⇒ E꜀ = 99 − 105

⇒ E꜀ = −6 units/min

⇒ The negative sign indicates that Pipe C is an emptying pipe.

⇒ Time taken by Pipe C to empty the completely filled cistern = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time = 4950 ÷ 6

⇒ Time = 825 min

**∴ The correct answer is 825 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours and another can empty it in y hours (where y > x), then the net part of the tank filled in 1 hour is (1/x) − (1/y).

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done. If multiple people work for the exact same number of days, their wages are divided in the direct ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Working

When workers or pipes operate on alternate days or hours, calculate the combined work done in one complete cycle before multiplying it to approach the total required work without exceeding it.
